title: Esteve CDMO invests US$80M to expand manufacturing operations in China | HealthCare Middle East & Africa - No.1 Health & Pharma Manufacturing Industry Publication

contentHtml:
CHINA—Esteve CDMO will invest US$80 million to relocate, modernize and expand its manufacturing operations in Shaoxing, China, as the Spanish contract development and manufacturing organization strengthens its production capacity and presence in Asian markets.

The investment will fund a new manufacturing site featuring three workshops, with an additional 150 m³ of reactor capacity reserved for future development.

Once expanded, the facility could have a total reactor volume exceeding 400 m³, increasing the company’s capacity to develop and manufacture active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).

Joan Petit, president of Esteve CDMO, described the investment as an important step in the continued development of the company’s global manufacturing network.

He said the expanded Chinese operations would bring its capabilities closer to customers across Asia while drawing on expertise from its international network.

Esteve strengthens its international manufacturing footprint

The China investment follows Esteve CDMO’s expansion into the United States.

In 2025, the company established a flagship US operation at its Morton Grove, Illinois, facility after acquiring Regis Technologies.

Although Esteve did not disclose the initial acquisition price, it has since committed an additional US$33 million to upgrade the facility.

The site provides services spanning early-stage research and development through API manufacturing, supporting pharmaceutical customers at different stages of product development.

The investments reflect a broader shift in the contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) sector.

Pharmaceutical companies increasingly require manufacturing partners that can support complex development programmes, scale production and serve markets across multiple regions.

In response, CDMOs are expanding their geographical reach and investing in specialized technologies and production capabilities.

CDMOs expand capabilities to meet changing drug development needs

Other manufacturers are pursuing similar strategies. Catalent has partnered with Ori Biotech to access Iro, an automated platform designed for cell therapy manufacturing.

The collaboration expands Catalent’s access to technologies intended to support more efficient production of advanced therapies.

Swiss CDMO Lonza has also announced plans to increase capacity to manufacture components used in antibody-drug conjugates (ADCs), with the longer-term goal of offering integrated services across the ADC production process.

Meanwhile, Belgium-based Ardena has expanded its service offering for biotechnology companies developing precision medicines.

Esteve CDMO said its integrated manufacturing network would help it meet the increasingly complex requirements of small-molecule API development and production for customers in China, other Asian markets and international markets.
